topIssues.title: Flaky test: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity (op-service/eth)
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Tracking a flaky failure in \`FuzzDetectNonBijectivity\` from \`op-service/eth\`.

### Symptom
\`\`\`
--- FAIL: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity (60.92s)
    fuzzing process hung or terminated unexpectedly while minimizing: EOF
    Failing input written to testdata/fuzz/FuzzDetectNonBijectivity/952a4f3fb88fb72c
    To re-run:
    go test -run=FuzzDetectNonBijectivity/952a4f3fb88fb72c
\`\`\`

### CI evidence
- Pipeline: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/125832/workflows/e3bdca63-068a-46ca-a424-fa4c4edae141/jobs/5084594
- Job: \`fuzz-golang-op-service\`, workflow \`main\`
- Branch at time of failure: \`aj/refactor/move-interop-messages-to-op-core\`

### Timing notes
32 workers; throughput collapsed from ~110 execs/sec to ~1/sec by 47s, stayed near 0 until \`-fuzztime\` (60s) expired, then parent reported a worker dying with EOF while minimizing. Other fuzz targets in the same job ran fine, so it isn't sustained job-wide starvation.

### Source
\`op-service/eth/blob_test.go:146\` — bit-flip non-bijectivity fuzz target seeded with deterministic \`rand\`.

A companion issue tracks the same symptom in \`FuzzEncodeDecodeBlob\` from the same job.

topIssues.title: flake: TestSequenceWindowExpired — 'must send tx: already known'
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filing this tracking issue from `/fix-flake`.

## Test
`op-e2e/actions/proofs.TestSequenceWindowExpired` (all matrix variants)

Package: `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-e2e/actions/proofs`

## Symptom

```
op-e2e/actions/helpers/user.go:288
    Error:      Received unexpected error:
                already known
    Test:       TestSequenceWindowExpired/HonestClaim-jovian
    Messages:   must send tx
```

The failure is in `(*BasicUser).ActMakeTx` — `eth_sendTransaction` returns `already known`, meaning the tx pool already had the tx (same hash). `require.NoError` then fails.

## Flake history (CircleCI Insights)

| Subtest | Flakes | Job |
|---|---|---|
| TestSequenceWindowExpired | 6 | go-tests-short |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired/JunkClaim-granite | 3 | go-tests-short |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired | 2 | go-tests-full |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired/JunkClaim-jovian | 2 | go-tests-short |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired/HonestClaim-granite | 1 | go-tests-full |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired/HonestClaim-granite | 1 | go-tests-short |
| TestSequenceWindowExpired/JunkClaim-granite | 1 | go-tests-full |

## Most recent failure

Job 5085890 on the merge-queue commit for PR #20893, subtest `HonestClaim-jovian`.

## Initial hypothesis

The test loop in `sequence_window_expiry_test.go:113` calls `env.Bob.L2.ActResetTxOpts(t)` then `env.Bob.L2.ActMakeTx(t)` in a tight loop. `ActMakeTx` builds a transaction using `PendingNonce` and signs it. If the prior iteration's transaction is still in the pool (recover mode skips inclusion) and the nonce hasn't advanced, the next iteration may build a tx with the same nonce / same signed bytes → `already known`.

Worth verifying against the actual `MakeTransaction` and `ActResetTxOpts` semantics, and against what RecoverMode does to inclusion.

topIssues.title: bug(op-reth): proofs-history exex SIGBUS crash and infinite retry loop during deep FCU rewinds
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The proofs-history exex has a race condition that causes **SIGBUS crashes** (exit code 135) during deep FCU-triggered rewinds, and an **infinite retry loop** that saturates logs and eventually makes the EL unresponsive. Both the deployed architecture (`LiveTrieCollector` + `spawn_sync_task`) and the new engine architecture on `develop` (`Engine`/`EngineState`) are affected.

Observed on sdg-v1 devnet on 2026-05-20 when an invalid cross-chain executing message triggered a 1,405-block deep reorg on chain 420120085. The bug manifested differently across four op-reth versions deployed simultaneously:

| EL Version | Symptom | 
|---|---|
| **v2.1.0-rc.1** | **SIGBUS crash (exit 135)** during FCU rewind → permanent CL/EL deadlock |
| **v2.2.0-rc.1** | Exex jammed on "Missing block 1880583" (thousands of retries/sec) → EL eventually unresponsive |
| **v2.2.2** | Exex jammed on "Missing block 1880582" (thousands of retries/sec) → log buffer saturated |
| **v2.2.3** | Appeared healthy — but only because the paired CL never triggered a rewind (bug still present in code) |

## Root Causes

### 1. `sync_target` is never lowered on rewind/unwind

**Old architecture (deployed):** `sync_target_tx` is a `watch::Sender<u64>` set in `handle_chain_committed` but never lowered in `handle_chain_reverted`. After a revert, the sync loop continues trying to fetch blocks up to the old (now-truncated) target.

**New architecture (develop):** `EngineState::update_sync_target()` at `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/state.rs:228-232` is monotonically increasing:

```rust
pub(crate) const fn update_sync_target(&mut self, block_number: u64) {
    if block_number > self.sync_target {
        self.sync_target = block_number;
    }
}
```

Neither `UnwindTask::run()` (`tasks/unwind.rs`) nor `ReorgTask::run()` (`tasks/reorg.rs`) reset `sync_target`. `handle_chain_reverted` in `lib.rs:376-389` sends an `Unwind` action but no `SyncTo` to lower the target.

### 2. No synchronization between static file truncation and mmap readers

The exex engine thread reads blocks via `provider.recovered_block()` which accesses reth's mmap'd static files (`StaticFileProvider`). When the main engine tree does `ftruncate()` on static files during a reorg, the mmap'd pages for blocks beyond the new file length become invalid. The exex thread reading those pages gets **SIGBUS** (kernel delivers bus error for pages no longer backed by the file).

There is no read-write lock, no notification, and no coordination between the truncation and the exex reader.

### 3. No backoff on retry when blocks are missing

**Old architecture:** On error, does `task::yield_now().await` then immediately retries.

**New architecture (develop):** The `crossbeam_channel::select!` fires `sync_rx` with `Duration::ZERO` when `needs_sync()` returns true. When `advance_sync()` fails with `BlockNotFound`, the error is logged and the loop immediately retries — **zero delay, full CPU spin**. This is actively worse than the old code.

```rust
// runner.rs, process_next_event():
recv(sync_rx) -> _ => if let Err(err) = self.advance_sync() {
    error!(target: "trie::engine::runner", ?err, "Sync step failed");
},
// immediately loops back, sync_rx fires again with Duration::ZERO
```

## Crash Timeline (from sdg-v1 incident)

Supernode CL detected an invalid executing message in block 1880582 and sent an FCU to rewind from block 1881986 → 1880581 (1,405-block deep reorg).

```
Time       Engine Tree (main)              ExEx Engine Thread
─────      ──────────────────              ──────────────────
15:33:50   FCU: rewind to 1880581          sync_target = ~1881986
  ...      Rewinding (20 seconds)          advance_sync() → block 1881200
  ...      (still rewinding)               advance_sync() → block 1881700
15:34:10   ftruncate() static files        advance_sync() → block 1881918
           pages beyond 1880581 gone       recovered_block() reads dead page
                                           "no state found" × 5,305
                                           "Missing block" × 392
15:34:14                                   *** SIGBUS (exit 135) ***
```

### Log evidence

**FCU timeout (20.25s, receiver dropped):**
```
ts=2026-05-20T15:34:10 level=warn target=engine::tree
  message="Failed to deliver forkchoiceUpdated response, receiver dropped (request cancelled)"
  state="ForkchoiceState {
    head_block_hash: 0xcbbe67f1...20075771,
    safe_block_hash: 0x4552f4f6...,
    finalized_block_hash: 0x4552f4f6... }"
  elapsed=20.250721856s
```

**Exex cascade (5,305 state errors + 392 missing block errors in 0.4s):**
```
ts=2026-05-20T15:34:10 level=error target=optimism::exex
  message="Batch processing failed"
  error="no state found for block 0xbf5a8d5698b1237b543371cb479871ccf9fd2bfa339e357dd4cf5dd226974335"
  id=proofs-history

ts=2026-05-20T15:34:10 level=error target=optimism::exex
  message="Batch processing failed"
  error="Missing block 1881918\n\nLocation:\n    op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs:381:32"
  id=proofs-history
```

**SIGBUS crash:**
```
Last State: Terminated
  Reason: Error
  Exit Code: 135   # = 128 + 7 (SIGBUS)
```

**Post-restart consistency check (static files at 1881985, DB at 1880580):**
```
Checking consistency for segment Headers
  initial_highest_block=1881985 highest_block=1880580
→ Setting unwind target = 1880580

Executing an unwind after a failed storage consistency check
  unwind_target=Unwind(1880580)
```

**Infinite retry loop on other nodes (saturates entire log buffer):**
```
ts=2026-05-20T16:39:17 level=error target=optimism::exex
  message="Batch processing failed"
  error="Missing block 1880582\n\nLocation:\n    op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs:381:32"
  id=proofs-history
# repeated thousands of times per second, pushing all other logs out of the buffer
```

## Impact

1. **SIGBUS crash** leaves the EL in an inconsistent state (DB unwound one block too far), creating a permanent CL/EL deadlock where the CL needs block N but the EL only has up to N-1
2. **Infinite retry loop** (thousands/sec) saturates log buffers, making debugging impossible, and eventually causes EL unresponsiveness through resource exhaustion
3. On the sdg-v1 devnet, this bug took down 3 of 4 supernodes. The only "healthy" one was never triggered because its CL lacked interop validation

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Reset `sync_target` on unwind (critical)

In `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/state.rs`, add to the `unwind()` method:

```rust
pub(crate) fn unwind(&mut self, to: BlockWithParent) -> Result<(), EngineError> {
    self.persistence.unwind(to, &self.memory)?;
    self.memory.unwind(to.block.number);
    // Reset sync_target so engine thread stops fetching truncated blocks
    self.sync_target = self.sync_target.min(to.block.number.saturating_sub(1));
    Ok(())
}
```

For the old architecture, `handle_chain_reverted` should send a lower value to `sync_target_tx`.

### Fix 2: Bounds check before `recovered_block()` (defensive)

In `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/runner.rs`, `advance_sync()`:

```rust
fn advance_sync(&mut self) -> Result<(), EngineError> {
    let current_tip = self.state.get_tip()?.number;
    if self.state.sync_target <= current_tip {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let block_num = current_tip + 1;
    // Don't read past what the provider actually has
    if block_num > self.state.provider.best_block_number()? {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let block = self.state.provider
        .recovered_block(block_num.into(), TransactionVariant::NoHash)?
        .ok_or(EngineError::BlockNotFound(block_num))?;
    // ...
}
```

### Fix 3: Add backoff on `BlockNotFound` errors

In `runner.rs`, the sync arm of `process_next_event()` should introduce a delay after errors instead of immediately retrying:

```rust
recv(sync_rx) -> _ => if let Err(err) = self.advance_sync() {
    error!(target: "trie::engine::runner", ?err, "Sync step failed");
    // Don't spin — wait before retrying
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1));
},
```

Or better: disable `sync_rx` until a new `SyncTo` action arrives.

## Affected Files

- `rust/op-reth/crates/exex/src/lib.rs` — `handle_chain_reverted` doesn't lower sync_target
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/state.rs` — `update_sync_target()` monotonically increasing, `unwind()` doesn't reset it
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/runner.rs` — `advance_sync()` no bounds check, `process_next_event()` zero-delay retry
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/tasks/unwind.rs` — `run()` doesn't reset sync_target
- `rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/engine/tasks/reorg.rs` — `run()` doesn't reset sync_target

## Additional Context

Full incident writeup with per-supernode analysis: https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Interop-Reorg-Test-Conductor-366f153ee16280089019f11abaf3e360

topPRs.title: refactor(interop): move interop message types to op-core/interop/messages
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Follow-up to #20884. Pulls the interop wire/message vocabulary out of `op-supervisor/supervisor/types` into a new `op-core/interop/messages` package, sibling to `op-core/interop/depset`. These types are the protocol surface spoken by op-node, op-supernode, op-interop-{filter,mon}, op-acceptance-tests, op-service RPC clients, and rust/kona test harnesses — they don't belong inside a deprecated component.

**Moved:** `BlockSeal` (+ helpers), `ExecutingMessage`, `Message`, `MessageChecksum`, `Identifier`, `ContainsQuery`, `Access`, `ExecutingDescriptor`, `ChecksumArgs`, `LogToMessagePayload`, `PayloadHashToLogHash`, `EncodeAccessList`, `ParseAccess`, `ExecutingMessageEventTopic`, and the access-list prefix constants.

**Left in `supervisor/types`** for now: `SafetyLevel` + its constants (separate stacked PR moves it to `op-service/eth`), `Revision`, `DerivedBlock*Pair`, `BlockReplacement`, `IndexingEvent`, and the supervisor backend sentinel errors. `supervisor/types` now imports the new package because `DerivedBlockSealPair` embeds `BlockSeal`.

**Caller sweep:** 37 leaf-only swaps, 66 mixed files (kept supervisor/types and added a second `messages` import).

Stacked on #20884.

topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Moves the interop result vocabulary (`ErrFuture`, `ErrConflict`, `ErrSkipped`, `ErrOutOfOrder`, `ErrDataCorruption`, `ErrAwaitReplacementBlock`, `GetErrorCode`, …) out of `op-supervisor/supervisor/types` into the top-level `op-core/interop` package. These sentinels are used across op-supervisor, op-interop-filter, op-supernode (activity tracker and raftwallogdb), and op-program (FPP consolidation), so they don't belong in op-supervisor.

`op-supervisor/supervisor/types/error.go` is deleted; the content lives inline in `op-core/interop/interop.go`.

Net result: `op-supernode/.../raftwallogdb` no longer imports any op-supervisor package.

Stacked on top of #20891.

topPRs.title: feat(op-deployer): allow ResourceConfig override per chain
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional, per-chain `ResourceConfig` override to op-deployer's `DeployOPChain` flow. Today the deploy script hardcodes `Constants.DEFAULT_RESOURCE_CONFIG()`, so chains that need a different gas envelope (notably any chain with `gasLimit < maxResourceLimit + systemTxMaxGas`, since the default sums to ~21M) cannot be deployed through op-deployer at all.

The override is opt-in: a zero-valued `maxResourceLimit` is treated by the Solidity script as "use the default", matching the pre-existing behavior. Setting any non-default value intentionally produces a chain that fails `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` (SYSCON-50…SYSCON-100) — this is documented in both the Go and Solidity comments.

### Changes

- **`state.ChainIntent`** — new optional `ResourceConfig` field with full `Check()` validation mirroring `SystemConfig._setResourceConfig` (precision, bounds, `uint128` cap, gas-limit headroom).
- **`opcm.DeployOPChainInput`** — new `ResourceConfig` ABI-bound struct. Adds `abiType:"uint128"` tag support so `MaximumBaseFee` (no native Go primitive) round-trips correctly.
- **`forge/encoding.go`** — `GoStructToABITuple` now honors an `abiType` tag for explicit Solidity type selection and recursively encodes nested struct fields as nested tuples.
- **`pipeline.DeployOPChain`** — converts intent → opcm struct; nil intent yields a zero struct (the Solidity sentinel for "use default").
- **`DeployOPChain.s.sol`** — adds `_resolveResourceConfig` and forwards the override to OPCM.
- **`Types.DeployOPChainInput`** — adds the `resourceConfig` field.

### Tests

- `state.TestChainIntentCheck_ResourceConfig` — table-driven coverage for every invariant (`maxResourceLimit > 0`, `elasticityMultiplier > 0`, denominator > 1, divisibility, `min ≤ max`, `uint128` bound, gas-limit headroom).
- `forge.TestGoStructToABITuple_AbiTypeTag` / `TestGoStructToABITuple_NestedStruct` / `TestBytesScriptEncoder_NestedAndUint128` — covers the new tag and nested-tuple encoding paths.
- `DeployOPChain_Test.test_run_resourceConfigDefaulted_succeeds` / `test_run_resourceConfigCustom_succeeds` — verifies a zeroed input still yields the default config and that a custom 5M-gas-limit chain initializes successfully.

topPRs.title: chore(op-node): remove op-supervisor support
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Removes the supervisor-managed code paths from op-node, leaving SuperAuthority (used by op-supernode) and the shared dependency-set plumbing intact. op-supervisor itself is going away in a follow-up; this PR just cuts op-node's coupling to it.

- Deletes `op-node/rollup/interop/` (the `IndexingMode` subsystem, RPC server, and `Config`/`Setup` plumbing) and the paired `L1TraversalManaged` derivation stage.
- Drops the `supervisorEnabled` toggles from `EngineController`, `Finalizer`, `AltDAFinalizer`; the `indexingMode` toggle from `DerivationPipeline` and `Driver`; the `ManagedBySupervisor` field on `SyncDeriver`; and the `InteropInvalidateBlockEvent` / `ProvideL1Traversal` event types.
- Removes `InteropConfig` from op-node config, the `--interop.rpc.{addr,port}` / `--interop.jwt-secret` CLI flags, the `NewSupervisorEndpointConfig` helper, and `OpNode.InteropRPC{,Port}` + the `interopSys` start/stop hooks. `--interop.dependency-set` stays (still used by derivation).
- Moves `InvalidatedBlockSourceDepositTx` + `OptimisticBlockDepositSenderAddress` into `op-node/rollup/derive/deposit_source.go` (op-program's FPP still needs them) and inlines the `-39003` interop-inactive RPC code in op-supervisor's `syncnode/rpc.go`.
- Rips the now-vestigial `InteropRPC()` interface, `interopEndpoint`/`interopJwtSecret` fields, and `tcpproxy` plumbing out of op-devstack (`stack/`, `sysgo/`, `presets/`) and the op-e2e opnode wrapper.

Stacked on #20889. 49 files, +213/−2261.

**Claude:** This PR was authored by Claude (an AI assistant) on behalf of Adrian.

## Description

Adds an acceptance-test topology where the light op-node CLs are the active sequencing nodes, while the shared supernode derives the safe and cross-safe chains.

This matches the intended infra shape:
- light CLs handle sequencing / unsafe-chain production
- the supernode remains non-sequencing
- proposer output is sourced from the supernode route
- the test verifies the supernode derives local-safe and cross-safe heads for blocks sequenced by the light CLs

Fixes #19389
